audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].side read 'Skill' while win[6] read 'Irelia' — the 2+ items row answered itself two ways.
audit.why: Phenomenal Evil Power grants permanent AP with no cap and Primordial Burst falls to 60s at rank 3 with missing-health scaling, so the late row is genuinely even rather than Irelia's. The other six rows agree across layers and match 51.23%.
audit.corrected: win[6] set to Skill to match the existing side, with phases[6].why and whys[6] rewritten to the even verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike stages named no cooldown numbers.
audit.why: Event Horizon 20/18.5/17/15.5/14, Baleful Strike 6s falling to 4s, Primordial Burst 120/90/60 at 650 range.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into cooldowns, carry, tldr and the late row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields told you to channel Defiant Dance through his burst. W reduces PHYSICAL damage only and Veigar's entire kit is magic.
audit.why: Irelia W text: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Baleful Strike, Dark Matter, Event Horizon and Primordial Burst are all magic damage.
audit.corrected: W-as-answer removed from tldr, phases[1].why, dosFull[0].t and dontsFull[0].d; the cage-edge rule kept, since that IS the decisive interaction and the page already had it right.

audit.why: The whole matchup is a cooldown race against a 20s Event Horizon.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late his passive AP never stops growing and Primordial Burst is 60s at rank 3 — even, if you can reach him.

edits.before: Late-game one-shot Q is real, but your gap-close speed and burst edge keep this in your favor
edits.after: Late this evens out: permanent stacks and a 60s Primordial Burst punish any approach that isn't a clean stun

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and 14s maxed — only the EDGE stuns, so walk toward its centre and never dash through the wall. - Baleful Strike is 6s at rank 1 and 4s maxed. - Primordial Burst at 650 range is 120s at rank 1 and grows with your missing health.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins, but Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only — every spell Veigar owns is magic.

edits.before: His combo is one window and your W shreds windows — channel the burst, dance the gap, and stun the cooldown silence.
edits.after: He owns one window — the cage edge — and no dash at all. Walk to its centre, wait the 20s out, then dash in and end it.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Veigar has no dash and no escape at all — once Flawless Duet lands he stands in it while you four-stack your autos on him.

edits.before: That is Veigar’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Defiant Dance is physical-only, so it does nothing to Baleful Strike or Dark Matter.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Baleful Strike reaches 1000 and permanently feeds his AP on kills — trading out there is paying his passive.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Dashing into the cage edge — Event Horizon stuns anything crossing that wall, and Primordial Burst follows.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage edge, then finishing with Dark Matter and Primordial Burst from 650 range.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by walking to the cage's centre, waiting out its 20s, then Q-resetting in — he has no dash to answer with.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Veigar's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the stacks: deny him Baleful Strike last-hits and all-in every time Event Horizon is on cooldown.

notes: The cage-edge rule already on the page is correct and was kept verbatim — it is the one inherited line in this matchup that beats the quality bar. Veigar's Dark Matter shows cd '0' in the kit file because Phenomenal Evil stacks reduce it; no fixed number was asserted anywhere as a result. breakdown.wave and breakdown.early remain Irelia-generic templates with nothing Veigar-specific to ground them in.
